newsitem.title: UK: E. Europe at less risk from tighter credit - EBRD.
newsitem.headline: E. Europe at less risk from tighter credit - EBRD.

text.p: Former communist countries in central and eastern Europe are at less risk from a possible global tightening in credit conditions than other emerging markets, the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) said.
EBRD first vice-president Ron Freeman told a news conference that history showed that "when financial markets tighten, emerging markets tighten first."
However, "these markets are less and less marginal," he said.
"The Czech Republic and several of the other countries have better credit ratings than countries that are already members of the European Union or donor countries of the EBRD."
Freeman mentioned Poland, Hungary and Slovakia as well as the Czech Republic.
"They may not be exposed to the same risk of the tide withdrawing first from the emerging markets because they have emerged to a very significant degree," he said.
There may have been some excessive or foolish lending to the region by western institutions in the past.
"I think the great majority of loans are in very good shape. That's certainly our experience," Freeman said.
"People are taking their borrowing obligations...very seriously. I think the lenders, by and large, who have made loans will be OK."
